cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where our office biscuits went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Wait. That's a clue, not a conclusion. I should announce the solution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them nobody eats until I identify the contents. Finding a box doesn't mean they've solved the biscuits.

mechanism: A asserts authority to stop information and eating until A can claim the first solution.
confusable: Unlike simply wanting biscuits, A makes every discovery a contest over who may announce and certify it.
comparison: A real office delivery creates a race against opening the box, unlike chalk-board chronology.
seedUse: The seed already forbids reading and eating and reserves announcement, giving S01 direct power claims over the competitive pursuit.
